candidate_whole: Redress architecture (routes to contest controllers/processors and supervisory authorities)
origin_of_candidate: seeded draw per DECISION_RULES §17 (seed 3037221655 over 13 eligible S: drawn SC-10)
I1_problem_scale: Which legally constituted routes let an individual contest conduct of controllers/processors and decisions or inaction of supervisory authorities, and how are the routes related? Function: adjudication/dispute resolution, remediation. Scale: instrument-level subsystem operating through Member State authorities and courts. Jurisdiction: Union instrument; national courts. Interval: baseline text applicable from 2018-05-25. Scope-fixing material: Arts 77–82, 12(4), 57(1)(f),(2), 58(4),(5), 60(7)-(9), 83(9)
I2_coupling: Internal (single S): conditional dependency 78(2)->77 (remedy for SA inaction conditional on a lodged complaint and a three-month period); information interface 77(2) and 12(4) (SA/controller must inform of judicial remedy); cumulative routes 78(1), 79(1) ('without prejudice to' administrative/non-judicial remedies and to the Art.77 complaint); representation 80(1) spans 77–79 and 82; forum rule 82(6)->79(2); mandatory interface 78(4) (SA forwards the Board opinion/decision to the court); SA referral/litigation 58(5) and fine initiation 83(9). Not accepted as coupling: common vocabulary of 'complaint' in 13(2), 14(2), 15(1), 41(2), 43(2) (false-positive members of the predicate)
I3_consequence: Property of the arrangement: multi-route redress: parallel routes (complaint; remedy vs controller/processor; remedy vs SA) plus a conditional escalation from SA inaction to a court (conditional sequence) with decentralised forums fixed by establishment/residence/SA seat. Bearer: S (configuration of routes), not any single relation. Rule: V6 §6.6 consequence types 'alternative route' and 'conditional sequence' (the property follows from the 'without prejudice' and conditional clauses, not from counts)
I4_boundary_objections: Coverage: all 389 paragraph units screened. Closure statement: within W no provision grants an individual a direct remedy against the Board — absence-dependent, valid for W only (Treaty-based review is outside W). External dependencies: content and procedure of remedies, court structure and the content of 'effective judicial remedy' are defined by Member State law (EXT register). Rival groupings: (a) complaint handling and fines belong to SC-02; (b) liability/compensation (Art.82) belongs to a private-enforcement S; (c) administrative and judicial redress as two separate S. Defeaters: Union-level remedies outside W; national procedural law
Q2_integration_assumed: No: the S was drawn by a text/pattern predicate (complaint/court), curated by inspection; the Chapter VIII heading was not used as evidence (Arts 83–84, penalties, are not part of the S)
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: Routes are related by conditional and cumulative clauses (relations between relations); counting remedies would not yield the conditional sequence
Q4_linking_rule: V6 §6.7 step 3 (configuration needs a theoretically specified combination of relationships) + I2/I3 as defined in v0.6.1 §6.2
Q5_alternative_grouping: Yes: complaint handling could be grouped with supervision (SC-02); both groupings fit the evidence; the overlap is recorded
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: Existence of the routes is stable under adding national law; the content/effectiveness of each route is not
kind_of_connection: qualified procedural dependency; conditional legal dependency; mandatory institutional interface (78(4))
outcome: Integrated architecture (simple case A=S) for the redress routes as stated in W; overlapping with SC-02/SC-07; content-level claims INDETERMINATE (external)
human_adjudication: Yes: whether cumulation ('without prejudice') is a configurational property; treatment of national procedural law

candidate_whole: Cooperation-and-consistency architecture among national supervisory authorities, the Board and the Commission
components: SC-07 (core: QR-0111–0116, 0133–0158, 0161–0181, 0197; Board tasks QR-0186–0194 peripheral; QR-0159 and QR-0160 (liability among Member States) are not members)
origin_of_candidate: deterministic rule per DECISION_RULES §17: eligible S with the largest number of distinct supporting units (100) = SC-07
I1_problem_scale: How is application of the Regulation kept consistent where several national authorities are competent? Function: cooperation/coordination, dispute resolution. Scale: Union-wide network of national authorities plus a Union body. Interval: baseline from 2018-05-25. Scope-fixing material: Arts 51(2)-(3), 56, 60–67, 68(3), 74(1)(b)
I2_coupling: Qualified procedural dependencies: 56(1)->60; 56(3): local SA informs LSA, LSA decides within 3 weeks; 60(3)-(6) draft decision and objection; 60(4)->63->65(1)(a); 64(1) six measures require a Board opinion; 64(6) standstill; 64(7)-(8)->65(1)(c); 65(2),(4),(6) binding decision, standstill, final decision bound; 61(8),62(7)->66(2); 66 urgency derogation. Integration through legally distributed decisions: binding Board decisions bind LSA and SAs concerned (65(2)); final decision of LSA is adopted 'on the basis of' the Board decision (65(6))
I3_consequence: Property of the arrangement: authority is distributed among national authorities at first instance and concentrated in the Board at the dispute stage (escalation path converting peer cooperation into vertical authority), with an urgency path allowing unilateral provisional measures subject to ex-post Board involvement. Bearer: S; and a positional property of the Board: final decision-maker among SAs within W (absence-dependent: valid for W only). Rule: V6 §5.2.1 dimensions (centralization; relational depth; discretion distribution) read per stage, no score
I4_boundary_objections: Coverage: full screening. External dependencies: the supervisory authorities are constituted by Member State law (N2: Arts 51(1), 54(1)(a)); EDPS (Board member) is constituted outside W; reviewability of Board decisions (Treaties) is outside W. Rival groupings: (a) split 60–62 (cooperation) from 63–67 (consistency); (b) include Board soft-law tasks 70(1) (weak coupling by task only). Defeaters: national derogations touching Chapters VI–VII (Arts 85(2), 90)
Q2_integration_assumed: No: the 'consistency' label is the Regulation's; coupling was taken from conditional cross-references, not from the heading of Section 2
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The escalation path exists only through the linkage of relations (60(4)->65); a count of cooperation relations would not show it
Q4_linking_rule: v0.6.1 §6.2 I2/I3; V6 §5.2.1 vertical distribution / centralization read per stage
Q5_alternative_grouping: Yes: cooperation (60–62) and consistency (63–67) as two S coupled by 60(4)->65 — consistent with the evidence; peripheral Board tasks as a distinct S
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: If the boundary included national law, SAs' instances and powers may differ; the type-level coupling stays; if Treaty remedies are included, 'final decision-maker' is weakened
kind_of_connection: qualified procedural dependency; conditional legal dependency; integration through legally distributed decisions
outcome: Integrated architecture (simple case A=S) at type level; peripheral Board tasks distinguishable; claims depending on national constitution of SAs or Treaty review INDETERMINATE
human_adjudication: Yes: classification of the procedures as devices (DEV threshold); the 'final decision-maker' claim

candidate_whole: Supervisory architecture (oversight/enforcement over controllers/processors integrated with cross-border consistency)
I1_problem_scale: How are monitoring and enforcement of compliance allocated to public authorities where processing is cross-border? Scale: Union instrument, national authorities. Scope-fixing material: Arts 55, 56, 57(1)(a), 58, 60(7)-(10), 65(6), 83
I2_coupling: Between-S coupling: competence allocation rules 55(1)-(2) (domestic cases) vs 56(1) (cross-border: lead authority) distribute cases between the two S; decisions towards controllers/processors under cross-border processing are products of the SC-07 procedure (60(3)-(7)); 65(6) binds the final decision to the Board decision; 64(1) makes several SA acts (lists, codes, BCR, clauses) conditional on a Board opinion. Kind: conditional legal dependency (cross-border condition) + qualified procedural dependency
I3_consequence: Conditional hierarchy: for cross-border processing the Board's binding decision constrains the LSA's final decision towards the controller (authority stratification); for domestic processing no such constraint (56(2), 55). Bearer: A (the combined arrangement), conditional on case type. Rule: V6 §5.2.1 centralization per case type; no score
I4_boundary_objections: Closure: absence of Board involvement for domestic cases is absence-dependent (W only). External: SA instances and powers by national law; Board decisions' reviewability. Rival: treat SC-02 and SC-07 as two distinguishable architectures with a conditional interface. Defeaters: national derogations (Arts 85(2), 90) modify SA powers for some processing
Q2_integration_assumed: No: integration is conditional on the cross-border criterion in the text
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The conditional hierarchy follows from how decisions in S1 depend on S2; it is not a property of either alone
Q4_linking_rule: v0.6.1 §6.2 (between-S coupling for a larger A)
Q5_alternative_grouping: Yes: two S with a conditional interface
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: If domestic-only processing were the corpus, SC-02 alone would be A; the integrated claim holds only for cross-border cases
kind_of_connection: conditional legal dependency; qualified procedural dependency; integration through legally distributed decisions (cross-border cases only)
outcome: Overlapping / partially integrated: integrated for cross-border processing, distinguishable (SC-02 alone) for domestic processing

candidate_whole: Private-assurance architecture (codes of conduct monitoring + certification)
origin_of_candidate: hypothesis on overlap (SC-05|SC-06 share 4 members); selected after the draw rule, not in place of it
I1_problem_scale: How is assurance by private intermediaries authorised and linked to public supervision? Scope-fixing material: Arts 40–43, 57(1)(m)-(q), 58(2)(h),(3), 64(1)(b),(c), 70(1)(n)-(p),(x), 83(2)(j),(4)
I2_coupling: Within each S: accreditation/approval by the SA, intermediary duties, reporting to the SA, revocation/withdrawal. Between S: (i) shared tasks and acts of the same authorities: 57(1)(p),(q) and 64(1)(c) treat accreditation requirements of both kinds of body in the same provision; (ii) shared downstream consumers: 24(3), 28(5), 32(3) (both as elements to demonstrate compliance), 83(2)(j) (both as fine-setting factor), 46(2)(e),(f) (both as transfer safeguards); (iii) shared sanction tier 83(4)(b),(c). Not found: any provision making a certification outcome relevant to code monitoring or conversely. Kinds: shared institutional participation; mandatory institutional interface (shared SA/Board acts); no conditional dependency between the S
I3_consequence: Candidate property: parallel routes for demonstrating compliance. Not uniform: 25(3) names certification only, 35(8) codes only. The property is therefore a feature of the downstream provisions, not of a coupled architecture of the two intermediary systems. No configurational consequence specific to the union of SC-05 and SC-06 was identified beyond what each S and the shared downstream provisions already state
I4_boundary_objections: External: national accreditation body (Reg. (EC) 765/2008, EN-ISO/IEC 17065/2012), national law constituting SAs. Rival: one 'assurance' architecture vs two. The label 'assurance' is a re-description supplied by the analyst (circularity risk) — the integrated claim is therefore not made
Q2_integration_assumed: The candidate was formed from the common function 'private intermediary assurance'; that is an analyst grouping — hence tested, and not accepted
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The only whole-level feature found is compositional (the same kind of arrangement twice)
Q4_linking_rule: v0.6.1 §6.2: shared actor/vocabulary/graph connectivity is insufficient
Q5_alternative_grouping: Yes: two distinguishable architectures with shared interfaces (preferred)
kind_of_connection: shared institutional participation; mandatory institutional interface (shared acts)
outcome: Overlapping (shared interfaces) — INTEGRATION INTO ONE ARCHITECTURE NOT SUPPORTED; treated as distinguishable architectures SC-05 and SC-06
human_adjudication: Yes: whether shared downstream use (24(3) etc.) is a coupling

candidate_whole: Commission rule-making architecture (delegated and implementing acts and their control)
I1_problem_scale: How is secondary rule-making allocated to the Commission and controlled? Scope-fixing material: Arts 12(8), 43(8), 92; 28(7), 40(9), 43(9), 45(3),(5), 46(2)(c), 47(3), 61(9), 67, 93
I2_coupling: Delegated acts: 92(2)-(5) (conferral, revocation, notification, objection) — complete within W. Implementing acts: every competence points to the examination procedure of Art.93(2) (or 93(3)); Art.93 incorporates Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 (not retrieved). Board advice to the Commission: 70(1)(b),(c),(q),(r),(s)
I3_consequence: For delegated acts: control of the delegate by the legislature (revocation, objection with consequence) — property of the delegation relation set (S). For implementing acts: the property of control depends on Reg. 182/2011 and cannot be stated within W
I4_boundary_objections: Decisive external dependency (Reg. 182/2011). Rival: two S (delegated vs implementing). Absence claims about control of implementing acts are not available
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: Delegation-plus-control is a relation set (revocation/objection over a conferral)
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: Including Reg. 182/2011 would change the finding for implementing acts
kind_of_connection: conditional legal dependency; qualified procedural dependency; integration through distributed powers (legislature–Commission)
outcome: INDETERMINATE overall (external dependency decisive for implementing acts); integrated (simple case) only for the delegated-act sub-arrangement

candidate_whole: Transfers architecture (routes for transferring personal data to third countries/international organisations)
I1_problem_scale: How is permissibility of third-country transfers organised across Commission, SAs and controllers? Scope-fixing material: Arts 44–50, 40(3), 42(2), 64(1)(d)-(f), 70(1)(s)
I2_coupling: Conditional legal dependency: 46(1) applies 'in the absence of a decision pursuant to Article 45(3)'; 49(1) applies in the absence of an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards (including BCR) — ordered fallback among routes; 46(3)-(4) SA authorisation through the consistency mechanism; 47(1) BCR approval through Art.63; 46(2)(d) clauses approved by the Commission; 46(2)(e),(f) link to Arts 40/42
I3_consequence: Ordered, conditional routing of authority among Commission (adequacy), SAs (authorisations, BCR), codes/certification and controller derogations: property of the set of routes (sequence and priority). Bearer: S. Rule: V6 §6.6 'sequence' and 'substitutability' read as a legal fallback order
I4_boundary_objections: External: third-country authorities, Directive 95/46/EC decisions retained (45(9), 46(5)), Reg. 182/2011 for implementing acts, EN standards. Rival: three separate S (adequacy, safeguards, derogations). Absence-dependent claims about third-country bodies not available
Q2_integration_assumed: No: ordering is stated in the text
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The fallback order is a relation among routes
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: Stable for the legal ordering; unknown for actual operation
kind_of_connection: conditional legal dependency; qualified procedural dependency
outcome: Integrated architecture (simple case A=S) as a legally ordered set of routes; operation and third-country elements INDETERMINATE
human_adjudication: Yes (mapping to the intermediation codebook's inter-architecture relation is a reading only; not verified with its authors)

candidate_whole: Multilevel supervisory architecture (national constitution and independence of SAs + Union-level organisation + cooperation/consistency + oversight)
I1_problem_scale: How is supervisory authority distributed vertically between national authorities and a Union body? Scale: Union/Member State. Scope-fixing material: Arts 51–58, 60–76
I2_coupling: Between-S coupling: 51(2) duty to cooperate through Chapter VII; 51(3) designation of the authority representing others in the Board and mechanism for compliance with Art.63 rules; 52(4) resources 'including those to be carried out in the context of mutual assistance, cooperation and participation in the Board'; 58(6) additional national powers 'shall not impair the effective operation of Chapter VII'; 68(3)-(4) composition of the Board from heads of national authorities; 69 independence of the Board
I3_consequence: Property: vertical distribution with national first-instance competence (55–56), national constitution (N2, 51/54) and independence, and Union-level binding resolution (65). Bearer: A (the combined arrangement). Rule: V6 dimensions vertical distribution/centralization/decision-centre plurality, stated per function
I4_boundary_objections: Decisive external dependency: national law constitutes each SA (instances, multiplicity, powers beyond Chapter VI); the Board's own establishment is N1 (68(1)); the EDPS is constituted outside W. Counts of decision centres: not computable (legal multiplicity 'one or more' per Member State; PT-7). Rival: two architectures (national; Union)
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The property depends on relations between the national and Union levels
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: If national law were in W, instances and multiplicity would be determinable; claims on decision-centre plurality are undetermined at type level
kind_of_connection: mandatory institutional interface; integration through legally distributed powers and duties; shared institutional participation (Board membership)
outcome: Integrated architecture (multi-S) at type level; INDETERMINATE for instances, multiplicity and national powers
human_adjudication: Yes: mediated constitution (Union obligation -> national constitution) is not covered by N1–N4

candidate_whole: Whole GDPR as one architecture (W = A)
origin_of_candidate: the hypothesis that the directive tells us to test and not to assume
I1_problem_scale: If the problem is Art.1's 'protection of natural persons with regard to processing and free movement of personal data', the scale is the entire instrument — too broad to be a governance question that one configuration organises
I2_coupling: A connected cluster exists around the SA/Board (SC-02, 05, 06, 07, 09, 10, 13, 14) through the interfaces recorded in AI-02/03/04/06/07. Regulated-side S (SC-01, 03, 04, 15) relate to the cluster through information and oversight relations with the SA (e.g. 30(4), 31, 33, 36, 37(7), 39(1)(d)-(e), 58(1)) but are not coupled to Commission rule-making (SC-08) except through advice and acts. Member State specification S (SC-11) is coupled by notification duties and by derogation clauses 85(2), 90
I3_consequence: A candidate whole-level property ('multilevel and intermediated supervision of a risk-based self-regulatory system') is a re-description of the union of S and was identified from the presence of those S: its identification presupposes the integration to be tested (circular). No property was found that is attributable to the whole W and not to S or to the SA/Board cluster
I4_boundary_objections: Coverage full; external references 22 unresolved; national derogations (85(2), 90) make the instrument's own scope conditional; rival groupings abundant
Q2_integration_assumed: Yes at the stage of the candidate whole (hence rejected)
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: No whole-level property found beyond composition
kind_of_connection: shared institutional participation; coordination; some qualified dependencies — not integration of the whole
outcome: W = A NOT SUPPORTED. Overlapping / partially integrated: a supervisory cluster (AI-02, 03, 07) plus distinguishable architectures; whole-instrument integration INDETERMINATE
human_adjudication: Yes (decision on I1: whether a whole-instrument question can be a legitimate governance problem)

candidate_whole: Controller-centred compliance arrangement with layered enhancement (V6 'enhanced self-regulation' pattern)
components: SC-15 + SC-03 + SC-04 + SC-05 + SC-06 + SC-02 (as public backstop)
origin_of_candidate: tests V6 §5.2.2 / §6.7 rule: enhanced self-regulation requires meaningful self-regulatory capacity AND institutionalized enhancement by relatively autonomous third parties
I1_problem_scale: How is production of compliance organised on the regulated side and how is it enhanced and backstopped? Scale: Union instrument, regulated organisations. Scope-fixing material: Arts 5(2), 24, 25, 28, 32, 35, 37–39, 40–43, 58, 83
I2_coupling: Self-regulatory capacity: risk-based 'appropriate measures' (24(1), 25, 32(1), 35(1)). Enhancement by relatively autonomous third parties: monitoring bodies (41(2)(a) independence) and certification bodies (43(2)(a) independence), but both are OPTIONAL: codes 'may', certification 'voluntary' (42(3)). Coupling of enhancement to the controller's position: 24(3), 28(5), 32(3), 35(8) (elements to demonstrate compliance), 83(2)(d),(j) (enforcement consequence). Internal enhancement: DPO independence 38(3), monitoring tasks 39(1)(b). Public backstop: 58, 36, 83
I3_consequence: Property: self-regulatory autonomy with optional layers of enhancement and a public backstop. The 'enhanced self-regulation' property of V6 is attributable to controllers that adhere to codes/certification (conditional), not to the instrument as a whole
I4_boundary_objections: External: NAB (Reg. 765/2008); national constitution of SAs; practice (not assessed). Rival: V6's meta-regulation pattern (Arts 24, 35 systems duties; 36 prior consultation) fits equally; patterns coexist (V6 §5.2.3)
Q2_integration_assumed: No: the V6 rule itself states the necessary conditions; evidence evaluated against them
Q3_configurational_vs_compositional: The optionality (42(3), 40(2)) makes enhancement conditional — a relation between the controller's choice and the layer
Q4_linking_rule: V6 §6.7 (enhanced self-regulation requires both conditions); v0.6.1 I2/I3
Q5_alternative_grouping: Yes: meta-regulation, enforced self-regulation and enhanced self-regulation coexist
Q6_boundary_sensitivity: Stable at the legal level; operation not assessed
kind_of_connection: conditional legal dependency; mandatory institutional interface (SA backstop)
outcome: Overlapping / partially integrated: enhanced self-regulation present as a CONDITIONAL layer (for adherents), together with meta-regulatory and enforced-self-regulatory elements; not a property of the whole instrument
human_adjudication: Yes: whether optionality defeats the 'institutionalized enhancement' condition
